correctness.rationale: Exact local AND/OR update conditioned on the hub and strict hub-majority thresholds yield an iff description of every hub-flipping two-cycle; stationary hub cases force the two step-two components to be full/empty, giving exactly two additional even-rim cycles. Labelled run counts are derived by compositions with a marked run, and exceptional n=3,4 cases are handled. Independent direct graph simulation covers 524272 states on rim lengths 3..17; an integer combinatorial checker confirms polynomial coefficients for component sizes 2..13 and values n3..60. Finite checks are corroborative; proof covers all n>=3.

originality.rationale: The wheel-specific two-cycle count, including a strict hub-flip coefficient region and the two stationary-hub cycles at even rim lengths, is not implied by the period-two theorem, the published one-dimensional cyclic fixed-point formula, tree-only classifications, or the cited MAX/MIN counts. Exact source comparisons and residual full-text priority limits are recorded.
residual_risks: The 1980 Goles–Olivos original article was not accessible in full; an exact specialized formula therein was not checked, though its available abstract addresses a general period bound rather than a wheel census.

value.rationale: This gives a complete exact primitive two-cycle census for a natural planar wheel family, separating stationary and alternating hub mechanisms. The globally thresholded hub couples local AND/OR updates into a nontrivial weighted run-count cutoff not provided by classical period-length bounds, and implies provably exponentially rare periodic states alongside exponentially many temporal cycles on infinite subsequences.
